samples.summary: OfflineRuntime housekeeping is the one offline surface NOT gated on `supportsClientKey()`, so every authenticated session pays for it while the feature is dark
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`, and `packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts` requires 0.7.23 — so `supportsClientKey()` is false on this build and no durable client can ever mount, meaning the store is always empty. The Settings section (`app/settings/page.tsx:118`) and the chip's offer (`sync-status-chip.tsx`) are both behind `supportsClientKey()`, but `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` mounts `<OfflineRuntime>` unconditionally and its effect (offline-runtime.tsx:54-140) opens/creates the IndexedDB database, runs `collectStale()`, and issues an extra unscoped `await fetchDocuments()` — `GET /documents`, which the backend fans out across every workspace the user belongs to (`packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:181-195`) — on every authenticated session, for a feature that cannot store anything. The `supportsClientKey()` gate the design calls a hard precondition is absent here.

samples.summary: `deleteDocuments`' new comment/defensive branch describes a partial-delete contract the backend does not have
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:419-437`: `POST /documents/delete` throws `ForbiddenException` if ANY id is not manageable and otherwise returns `{ deleted: body.ids }` — all-or-nothing. The new comment ("The route is manager-gated per id, so a partial answer is ordinary") and the `result.deleted ?? []` fallback describe a response shape this endpoint never produces, and the new test `documents.test.ts:157` pins a behaviour the server cannot exhibit. Harmless at runtime, but the comment will mislead the next change to either side.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` gain two extra API round trips each (including a cross-workspace document listing) on a path whose existing callers just mutate-and-invalidate
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn` (workspaces.ts:101-114) now calls `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus the unscoped `fetchDocuments()` before the DELETE. The existing callers are `packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:133` (`removeMember`) and `:182` (`deleteWorkspace`), which run these as mutations with a spinner; both now block on a full `GET /documents` across every workspace the caller belongs to. The workspace-scoped `fetchWorkspaceDocuments` already exists at workspaces.ts:290 but lists only the workspace root (`folderId ?? null`, backend controller:155-159), so it is not a drop-in — worth recording that reasoning at the call site rather than leaving the unscoped listing looking accidental.

samples.summary: The shared-PDF layout mounts its own YorkieProvider outside `NonDurableScope`; only the `pdf-` docKey prefix keeps share-link PDF content off a visitor's disk
samples.evidence: `shared-document.tsx:1016` wraps the doc/slides/note/board/sheet branch in `NonDurableScope`, but `SharedPdfLayout` (shared-document.tsx:736-792) mounts `<YorkieProvider>` → `<PdfCollabProvider>` outside it. Today this is safe only because `PdfCollabProvider` uses `docKey={`pdf-${documentId}`}` (app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200) and `use-durable-document.ts`'s `isExcluded()` refuses `pdf-` keys. The design claims two independent defences for share links; on this path there is one, so relaxing the PDF exclusion (e.g. once PDFs get a sync chip) would silently make share-link PDF comment documents durable on a visitor's device. Searched every `CollabDocumentProvider` mount site (docs/notes/slides/board/document detail, pdf-collab, shared-document) — all owner routes are intentionally durable and this is the only unwrapped non-owner mount.
